summary: Anthropic announces an update to Claude Fable 5's biology safety classifiers that reduces false-positive fallbacks to a less capable model by about 85% for biology-related queries while continuing to block dual-use biology and drug-development requests.

mechanisms.reason: Fewer fallbacks to the less-capable Opus 5 means more queries are now served by the frontier Fable 5 model instead of being downgraded.
mechanisms.quote: In our testing, this update reduced biology-related fallbacks by about 85% across our product surfaces.

categories.reason: The safeguard update expands the range of clinical and health-related tasks Fable 5 can assist with, touching clinical workflows.
categories.quote: Healthcare professionals will be able to receive more support from Fable 5 on clinical tasks.

practices.reason: The post describes Anthropic's internal classifier constitution, training data and jailbreak-robustness process for safety classifiers, which is a described but non-transferable internal safety evaluation method.
practices.quote: We also require our classifiers to be robust to attempts to bypass them (known as jailbreaks), which requires even further research and testing.

practices.reason: Reduced fallback rates change the expected behavior and model-mix a downstream integration would observe when calling Fable 5 across product surfaces.
practices.quote: we expect the total number of fallbacks—for biology–related or any other reasons—will also be reduced: by roughly 67% on Claude.ai , 55% on Cowork, 17% on Claude Code, and 7% on the Claude Platform.
